claims.text: Adding approximately 2 at.% Dy to a CoFeNi-based high-entropy alloy will increase its coercive field.
Dy doping will create local lattice distortions in the CoFeNi-based alloy.
Dy doping may produce nanoscale precipitates or secondary domains.
Dy-induced lattice distortions and precipitates will provide additional domain-wall pinning sites.
Rare-earth doping will enhance local chemical and structural heterogeneity.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning will increase coercivity.
The Dy-doped alloy will have a coercive field at least 10–20% greater than the matched undoped alloy.
The predicted coercivity increase should occur after arc melting and homogenization under an inert atmosphere and when measured near 300 K.
Higher Dy concentrations may cause excessive second-phase formation.
Excessive second-phase formation at higher Dy concentrations may reduce overall magnetic performance.
The Dy concentration that maximizes the effect is unknown.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires an increase of at least 10–20%, but the falsification rule only rejects the hypothesis when there is no measurable increase or a decrease. An increase smaller than 10% would violate the quantified prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.

The intervention specifically predicts an effect at approximately 2 at.% Dy, whereas the falsification rule requires failure across all doped samples from 0–5 at.%. Thus, failure at the specified 2 at.% intervention would not necessarily falsify the hypothesis if another concentration increased coercivity.
